title: Brown Sugar Eggnog Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft eggnog cupcakes with brown sugar warmth take 25 minutes to prep and 18 minutes to bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a mug of eggnog on a snowy afternoon. Brown sugar adds a deep, caramel note that plain white sugar cannot give you. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen before the crumb turned out soft enough to match the nutmeg buttercream on top Eggnog goes right into the batter. Not just the frosting, so the flavor runs all the way through. A double hit of nutmeg and a little cinnamon keep things cozy without tasting like a spice cabinet. This is a classic holiday cupcake for cookie swaps, office parties, or a quiet night with hot cocoa. Make the batter ahead and frost the day you serve them for the best texture.
ingredients: 1 tbsp dark rum or 1/2 tsp rum extract (optional)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, salt, nutmeg, and cinnamon in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and brown sugar together for 2 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla.
Add the dry mix in three parts, alternating with eggnog and rum. Start and end with dry mix.
Mix just until batter is smooth. Do not overmix or cupcakes will turn dense.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 17 to 19 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar in two parts, beating well.
Add eggnog and nutmeg to the frosting. Beat 2 minutes until light and pipeable.
Cool cupcakes fully before frosting. Pipe frosting high and dust with extra nutmeg.
tips: Use full fat eggnog, not the light version. It keeps the crumb moist and adds real flavor.
Room temperature eggs and eggnog blend smoother and stop the batter from breaking.
If frosting looks thin, chill it 10 minutes before piping for a firmer swirl.
Bake a test cupcake first if your oven runs hot. Eggnog batter browns fast on the edges.

faq.question: Can I use store bought eggnog in this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes, any store bought eggnog works well. Choose a full fat version for the richest flavor and best crumb.

faq.question: Do these cupcakes taste boozy?
faq.answer: No, the rum is optional and small in amount. It only adds warmth, not a strong alcohol taste.

faq.question: Can I make the cupcakes ahead of the holiday party?
faq.answer: Bake cupcakes one day ahead and store covered at room temperature. Frost them the day you serve for the freshest look.

faq.question: Why did my eggnog cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means overmixed batter or an underbaked center. Mix just until smooth and test with a toothpick at 17 minutes.

conclusion: These brown sugar eggnog cupcakes bring the whole holiday season into one bite. Bake a batch for your next cookie swap and watch them disappear first.
